caep.broadcast_failed: The signal could not be broadcast. An event type and a subject are both required.
caep.broadcast_help: Sent to every active OIDC client. Recorded in the audit trail with the reason you give.

help.account-disabled: Tells receivers the account is disabled. Broader than a session revocation: it asks them to stop accepting the subject entirely.
help.credential-change: Tells receivers a credential changed — a password reset or a new authenticator.
help.risky-login: Tells receivers a sign-in looked risky, so they can step up or re-evaluate their own session.
help.session-revoked: Tells receivers to end the subject's sessions. Use after a compromise or a forced sign-out.

caep.history_help: From the audit trail, so it records what was requested rather than what arrived.
caep.inbound_none_body: This deployment transmits shared signals but does not receive them: there is no inbound RISC/CAEP endpoint, so third-party account-compromised or account-disabled signals are not accepted or stored. An empty inspector here would read as “no incoming threats” rather than “not listening”.
caep.reason_help: Recorded in the audit trail. Write what a colleague reading this in six months would need.
caep.simulated_body: The backend recorded and audited this signal, but marks each recipient as simulated: live push dispatch is not switched on, so no relying party has acted on it.
caep.stream_off_body: The shared signals stream is switched off in the SSF configuration. Broadcasts are still recorded in the audit trail but no receiver is configured to act on them.
caep.subject: Subject
caep.subject_help: Who the signal is about — an identifier the receivers can resolve, such as the email or subject id.
caep.subtitle: Broadcast CAEP and RISC security events to every registered relying party, and review what has been sent.
